If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract pessimism.

If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 3 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% for late horizon (16–30 days) to account for reversal risk.

If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for early horizon to capture momentum.

If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast for mid horizon to avoid false support.

If sentiment is mixed (±0.33) and forecast deviates >1.5% from recent history, apply a 0.5–1.0% correction in direction of sentiment dominance for late horizon.
